statement: Two independent connected paths with specified pairs of endpoints can have E I=N tending to infinity while P(I>0)=1/N tends to zero, where I counts their common vertices.
assumptions: Independent uniform corridor labels J,K in {1,...,N}
L=N^2 common vertices in each disjoint corridor
Four distinct source endpoints; only equal labels cause intersection
proof_or_counterexample: I=N^2 1{J=K}; E I=N, E I^2=N^3, P(I>0)=1/N. Separate binary endpoint fans also give maximum graph degree three.
remaining_gap: Independent referee check pending; these path laws are not asserted to be Ising current laws.

statement: If centered real X_n have E X_n^2=1 and E X_n^4<=3-delta for fixed delta>0, every weak subsequential limit is centered, has variance one and fourth moment at most 3-delta, and is non-Gaussian.
assumptions: Centered real random variables
Variance one for every n
Uniform positive fourth-moment deficit
Scalar weak subsequential convergence
proof_or_counterexample: The fourth-moment bound gives uniform integrability of first and second moments. Truncating x^4 and then monotone convergence gives the upper bound for the limit fourth moment. Compare with fourth moment three for N(0,1).
remaining_gap: Independent check pending; no random-distribution tightness or Ising overlap lower bound follows.

statement: For a finite free-boundary zero-field ferromagnetic Ising model and weights f_x>=0, let V=E(sum f_x sigma_x)^2>0. Under Q_f(x1,...,x4)=f1 f2 f3 f4 G12 G34/V^2, E X_f^4=3-2 E_Q p, where p is connection of x1 to x3 in the original union of two currents with parity source pairs 12 and 34.
assumptions: Finite graph, zero field, nonnegative couplings, free boundary
Nonnegative nonzero weights
Source sets are modulo two
Define p arbitrarily, e.g. zero, on zero-Q tuples with unsupported sources
proof_or_counterexample: Sum -U4=2 G12 G34 p with the four weights; each of the three pair-products sums to V^2. Q has total mass one. Finite chain verification covers all 4^4 endpoint tuples at three couplings.
remaining_gap: A scale-independent lower bound on E_Q p for actual critical 3D currents is unproved; connection to the source near-critical g requires cutoff and normalization control.

statement: On the three-edge Ising path 0-1-2-3 at parameter t>0, a current with sources {0,1} hits vertex 2 with probability 1-sech(t), whereas that source component after one independent sourceless augmentation hits 2 with probability tanh(t)^2. The standard two-point hitting identity cannot be used as an equality for the bare current.
assumptions: Finite path, free boundary, zero field
Positive coupling parameter t
Current weights product t^n/n! subject to source parity
source: owner-own-work: VERIFICATION.json and ATTEMPT.md; primary law attribution Aizenman (5.9)
proof_or_counterexample: The bridge edge is even. Its conditional probability of zero is 1/cosh(t); two independent even currents both vanish with probability sech(t)^2. At t=0.1 the probabilities are 0.004979251046773414 and 0.009933709152560035.
remaining_gap: Independent reviewer pending; no dimension-specific estimate claimed.

statement: For finite ferromagnetic trees at zero field and free boundary, original two-source-current connection q and meeting r of the independently sourceless-augmented source components satisfy q >= (e/4) r^2. The constant is asymptotically sharp among paths.
assumptions: Finite connected tree
Source-pair current measures exist
Four independent currents with source pairs ab,cd,empty,empty
No cyclic-graph transfer
source: owner-own-work: TREE_NONLINEAR.md; derived after reading and independently checking w468 TREE_OBSTRUCTION.md
proof_or_counterexample: If source paths meet, q=r=1. Otherwise q=product p_i and r=q(1+sum(1-p_i)); 1-p_i<=-log p_i and max_(x>=0)(1+x)e^(-x/2)=2/sqrt(e) give the bound. Paths p_i=e^(-1/m) approach equality.
remaining_gap: w470 independent check pending; analogous inequality on the full critical Z^3 lattice is unproved.

statement: For a sourceless random current on a uniform four-edge cycle at t>0, the odd-edge indicators are all the same Bernoulli variable of parameter h=tanh(t)^4/(1+tanh(t)^4). Hence E[B_e B_f]=h>h^2=E B_e E B_f for distinct edges; conditioning on the source set alone does not give independent edge values.
assumptions: Finite four-cycle, zero field, free boundary
Positive uniform parameter t
One current with empty parity source set
proof_or_counterexample: The source constraint allows exactly the all-even and all-odd parity vectors. Their weights are cosh(t)^4 and sinh(t)^4. The odd indicators coincide with the sector bit. This invalidates transplanting tree edge factorization to cyclic graphs.
remaining_gap: No cyclic-graph nonlinear comparison or 3D original-current connection lower bound is proved.

statement: For homogeneous zero-field nearest-neighbor Ising on Z^3 at 0<beta<beta_c, let R=ceil(xi), B_R=[-R,R]^3 intersect Z^3, and chi_R=sum_(x in B_R)G(0,x). Sample independent x2 and y on B_R with weights G(0,x)/chi_R and x3 uniformly on B_R, put x4=x3+y, and let p be the thermodynamic limit of the original two-current connection probability for (0,x2,x3,x4). Then -g(beta)>=2 |B_R|/xi^3 (chi_R/chi)^2 E p. A lower bound (chi_R/chi)^2 E p>=epsilon>0 along beta_n increasing to beta_c suffices for the literal C0052 source criterion.
assumptions: Homogeneous nearest-neighbor ferromagnet, zero field, free-boundary thermodynamic state
0<beta<beta_c so chi and xi are finite and xi>0
g and exponential xi as in source equations (7.1)-(7.2)
Thermodynamic limit first, fixed endpoints and beta; finite-volume switching and convergence of spin correlations
proof_or_counterexample: All summands of -U4 are nonnegative. Retain x2,x3,y in B_R with x4=x3+y, and use -U4=2G(0,x2)G(x3,x3+y)p. Translation invariance gives total sampling mass |B_R|chi_R^2. Divide by chi^2 xi^3. Since |B_R|=(2ceil(xi)+1)^3>=8xi^3, the quantitative input gives -g>=16epsilon along the sequence.
remaining_gap: The displayed positive lower bound is still unproved for the actual near-critical 3D law; neither a susceptibility-mass floor nor a current-intersection floor is assumed proved. No critical-field all-subsequence statement follows automatically.
